deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page continues the previous one. There Riemann shows that a function with the defining properties of his P-function satisfies y'' + p y' + q y = 0 with single-valued p and q. He then asks where p and q become infinite. The page is a draft of the argument that leads to the exponent condition alpha+alpha'+beta+beta'+gamma+gamma' = 1 in the 1857 paper 'Beitraege zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(alpha,beta,gamma,x) darstellbaren Functionen'. The next page begins with the symbol P(alpha,alpha'; beta,beta'; gamma,gamma'; x).

(1) Aim. Riemann first wants to show that for no value other than 0, infinity and 1 does the denominator (the Wronskian) vanish. That is, he wants to rule out apparent singularities.

(2) First attempt (struck through with a large pencil X). The domain is all complex x except:
- the real values < 1 (a slit through 0 and 1, which would make the branches single-valued);
- the small neighbourhoods |x| < eps, |1/x| < eps', |1-x| < eps''.

(3) Second version. Riemann drops the slit. He switches to the independent variable t = log x and writes the equation as d^2y/dt^2 + p dy/dt + q y = 0. With the log-Wronskian W = y1 dy2/dlog x - y2 dy1/dlog x he states
  p = - d log W / d log x.
[Mine: this is Abel/Liouville. Eliminating q from the equations for y1 and y2 gives dW/dt = -pW. Also W_log = x*W_x and p_log = x*p_x - 1.]

Under a circuit, y1 and y2 undergo a linear substitution with determinant ad-bc nonzero. So W is multiplied by a constant, and d log W, hence p, is single-valued. This is why the slit is no longer needed.

(4) Domain S. S is the x-sphere minus three small discs: |x| < eps, |1/x| < eps', |1-x| < eps''. Riemann considers the boundary integral of p d log x over the boundary of S.

By Cauchy's theorem, the integral is unchanged if one removes from the interior of S regions in which the integrand stays continuous.

(5) Singularities inside S. log W, and hence p, is discontinuous only where W is infinite or zero. Riemann assumes this happens at points a', a'', a''', ... with W comparable to (x-a')^{lambda'}, (x-a'')^{lambda''}, ... (W/(x-a)^lambda stays finite and nonzero).

A marginal insertion justifies this: y1 and hence W vary continuously and single-valuedly in S (up to the constant factor).

(6) Residue count. Shrinking S to small circles around the a's gives
  integral of p d log x = 2 pi i * sum(lambda) (Riemann's sign).
The page breaks off ('durch Integral') before the boundary integral is evaluated a second way, namely from the local exponents at 0, 1, infinity.

[Completion, mine, as in the published paper and the Nachlass. At 0, W ~ x^{alpha+alpha'}. At 1, W ~ (1-x)^{gamma+gamma'-1}. At infinity, W ~ x^{-(beta+beta')}. The argument principle on the whole sphere then gives
  sum(lambda) = 1 - (alpha+alpha'+beta+beta'+gamma+gamma').
Since W is holomorphic in S for a P-function, the lambda are nonnegative integers. So the exponent sum is at most 1, with equality iff there are no apparent singular points. This is Riemann's condition alpha+...+gamma' = 1, i.e. the Fuchs relation for three singular points.]
errors: Sign: with the boundary positively oriented, p = -dlog W/dlog x gives integral of p dlog x = -2 pi i * sum(lambda). Riemann writes +2 pi i * sum(lambda); this is either an orientation convention (boundary traversed with the domain on the right) or a sign slip.
First draft writes 'Modul von x/1 < eps' (apparently an x/eps or x/1 slip); it is corrected in the second version to 'Modul von x < eps'.
The argument is incomplete on this page: the evaluation of the boundary integrals around 0, 1, infinity is not carried out, and the text breaks off.
Previous page (context, not this page): the formula for p lacks the minus sign, and the denominator has y2 dy2/dx where y2 dy1/dx is meant.
Implicit assumption: the a', a'' are finitely many with algebraic-type behaviour; this is stated as an assumption ('Ich nehme an'), not proved.

results.what: p = -d log W/dt for the Wronskian W in the variable t = log x, and single-valuedness of p because monodromy multiplies W by det(ad-bc)

Counting zeros/poles of the Wronskian by the contour integral of p d log x over the sphere minus discs around 0, 1, infinity, to show no apparent singularities occur and to obtain the exponent condition
results.modern_name: Fuchs relation (sum of exponents = number of singular points - 2 + number of apparent singularities) via the argument principle
results.usually_credited_to: L. Fuchs (1866) in general; Riemann 1857 for the three-point P-function condition, with the general version in his Nachlass ('Zwei allgemeine Lehrsaetze ueber lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten', Werke 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the argument behind the alpha+...+gamma'=1 condition of Riemann's 1857 P-function paper. The general Wronskian and argument-principle approach also appears in his published Nachlass on linear ODEs with algebraic coefficients. The interest is in seeing the draft: the abandoned slit domain, the switch to the log x variable, and the explicit admission of possible extra zeros a', a''. No new result is involved.

checkable.asserts: For the hypergeometric equation the Wronskian is x^(-c)(1-x)^(c-a-b-1), i.e. dlogW/dx = -p (Abel).
The Gauss equation's exponents at 0 (0, 1-c), 1 (0, c-a-b) and infinity (a, b) sum to 1: Riemann's condition with no apparent singularities.
The log-Wronskian near 0 behaves like x^(alpha+alpha'), giving a residue contribution alpha+alpha'.
In the variable t = log x, W_log = x W_x and p_log = x p_x - 1, consistent with p_log = -dlog W_log/dlog x.

checkable.sympy: al,alp,be,bep,ga,gap=symbols('al alp be bep ga gap'); s_lambda=-(be+bep)-(al+alp)-(ga+gap-1); simplify(s_lambda-(1-(al+alp+be+bep+ga+gap)))==0
checkable.asserts: Argument-principle count (completion of the page): the extra zeros satisfy sum(lambda) = 1 - (sum of the six exponents).

transcription_corrections: In the second version the condition reads 'Modul von x < eps' (the first, struck version has a fraction, x over something, struck or garbled).
The first excluded-region version (lines 3-10) is cancelled by a large pencil X and long ink strokes; it is not part of the final text.

Marginal insertion at right: 'Da die Function y_1 und folglich die Function (y1 dy2/dlogx - y2 dy1/dlogx) im Gebiete S stetig und einwerthig sich aendert' - the word read as 'unstetig' is struck, and the region label is likely 'S'.
There is a marginal 'E'' (or similar) mark at the right; the final 'Sigma lambda' in the integral formula has an attached superscript-like mark, probably the index of lambda.
